themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the system often changes while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Today's journey orchestration answers open with a person-level holdout and a shared ledger of what was actually sent, echoing the identity resolution panels of known people, the repeating buyer-question panels for answer engines, the always-on geo holdouts for incrementality, and the admission in B2B buying-group intent that a lost signal and a signal that never existed look identical.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: In today's journey orchestration answers all three models land on channel owners whose bonuses and credited conversions make coordination an act of self-harm, matching the agent traffic answers that build a fast lane so declaring beats spoofing, the semantic layer answers calling definition fights a political power struggle, and the measurement and ad supply answers pointing at platforms that profit from opacity.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: The content governance answers keep landing on implied claims that no registry holds and no classifier reliably sees, while the semantic context layer answers insist that conflicting definitions of active customer are legitimate rather than wrong, and today's orchestration answers say no objective function can price a sale today against fatigue tomorrow.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: The downstream consent answers agree that black-box ad networks and already-trained models cannot show person-level deletion without retraining, which repeats in identity resolution where closed platforms hide false matches, in answer engine work where retrieval and weights are unreadable, and in ad supply integrity where fabricated impressions and real performance look the same.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: The agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with hard spend, rate and audience caps because sends and spend have no rollback, the consent answers put one checkpoint in front of every data exit, and today's orchestration answers propose a shared ledger or kill switch that can only veto outgoing messages.
